seat.BEST_WHY: The wall run at y≈388–455 is built as two distinct planes with a hard, unbroken separator line at y≈424 carried the full width from x≈190 to x≈750, and a second contact line at y≈455 where it meets the floor. Both planes are coursed, and the block widths along the near band vary (roughly 10, 14, 20 and 26px between x 300 and 480) so the run reads as cut stone rather than a repeated stamp. The lighting holds structure under load: measured across x 190–560, y 450–600, only 16 pixels reach L≥240 and the peak is 208, so the mortar grid survives all the way into the brightest part of the pool — you can count courses across the whole lit floor. Falloff is also consistent between surfaces: the wall/floor luminance ratio stays in a 0.54–0.76 band from x=200 out to x=620 instead of jumping around. And the frame is genuinely sharp — the pins, rope lines and hatch-marks on the pier at x 440–640, y 60–390 are legible as individual marks.
seat.WORST_WHY: The water at x 248–343, y 0–191 is a rectangle. Square corners at (248,191) and (343,191), one flat green fill with a faint hex pattern, no bank, no shoreline, no depth shading, no wet dirt where it meets the ground — the dirt touching the water at y=189 is the identical dry brown as the dirt at y=60. The grey flagstone at x 0–55 and x 343–384 is one 16px stone stamped on a perfect grid with every joint at the same value and no wear anywhere. The crates at x 63–97, y 0–89 are drawn in three-quarter view with a visible front face, and the barrels at (127,203) and (176,203) show full elliptical tops plus a tall side, both sitting on a floor drawn straight from above. The lily pads are three sizes of one blob repeated eight times — (320,20), (311,36), (313,114), (326,124), (277,163), (263,180), (262,153), (308,133). And there is no light source in the frame at all: every pixel sits at ambient, with the sole exception of the brown ellipse under the green figure at (224,20), which is the only shadow anywhere in the image.

_what: THE ITEM'S OWN MEASURED EXIT — required by INSTALL-LATEST (Rafe, 2026-09-08).
A build installs because it DID THE THING IT SET OUT TO DO. The rank test only says
the doing cost nothing against the seeded reference; this says what was done. Without
it, 'not worse than the reference' would mean 'not different from it', and a round
that changed nothing would install as readily as one that fixed something.
Declared here per item, recorded into the verdict, re-checked at the gate. The gate
refuses a `met` with no measurement behind it.
item_exit.item: #198 — the shoulder's remaining share of the halo, measured on what it scales BY
item_exit.claim: the halo's residual is the shoulder compressing by ALBEDO, so a pale stone is squashed harder than the dark one beside it; scaling by the delivered LIGHT instead preserves that difference while still rolling the top end off
item_exit.measured: The shoulder must NOT go: nulled, the floor's p99 leaps 205.50 -> 247.85 and 1324 pixels pile within two levels of the max — the flat top §6.2 exists to prevent. And the KNEE is not the lever: 0.75 -> 0.88 on the old formulation buys 0.014 of ratio, because the knee only decides where compression starts while the ceiling decides how hard. WHAT IT SCALES BY IS THE LEVER. `m` was max(lit)*a — the composite, albedo included — so compression was a function of how bright the stone is, and the difference between neighbouring stones is the texture the halo eats. Scaling by `delivered` makes it a function of range instead: two stones at the same distance get the SAME scale and their ratio survives. Same argument as the specular fix — multiplying preserves Weber contrast, anything varying with albedo destroys it. MEASURED, core-to-mid contrast ratio on the props scene: shipped (composite) 0.644, shoulder NULLED 0.781, scaled by light 0.818 — BETTER THAN NULLING IT, because nulling lets the top saturate into a plateau that destroys contrast in its own way. Plateau (px within 2 of max): 16 shipped, 1324 nulled, 40 on light. Far field UNCHANGED (+0.00 at 3.5-4.2 tiles), which is the shader's own rule and is now structural rather than incidental: the knee sits on delivered light, which falls with distance, so distant fragments never reach it. THE COST, STATED: the mid-pool (1.2-2.8 tiles) is 9.6 levels darker, about 8%. Raising the knee recovers some of that and blows the plateau up — 0.82 gives 644 px and 0.88 gives 764 against 40 — so 0.75 stands on the new formulation too, for a different reason than before. The null is still exact: below the knee the scale is 1.0 by construction.
item_exit.instrument: null-control and knee-sweep arms on the props scene; core-to-mid relative contrast by radial ring, floor cells only; plateau counted as floor pixels within 2 levels of the frame's max

law: LOOP-PROCESS: an art round is judged by eyes on delivered frames. The plant must land worst-or-flagged; a passed plant voids the round and its findings are not read. The guards measure progress — rank in the deck — never rounds elapsed.

It is deliberate and owed: B-PROP-003's card splits the prop so the sprite RECEIVES and the engine EMITS, because a painted glow is §6.3's outlawed rim by another name.
